verdict.overall: GREEN on V1/V3/V4/V5 + mask-orientation + T-hammer; AMBER on V2 (auto-default rationale).

V1_strict_fits_cells.evidence: Natural-L strict 3/3 PASS (median fit 68.3, deep_overflow 0); T-hammer strict 2/3 PASS (median 67.5, seed 603=95.89 near-perfect, deep 0). Containment reproduced on the production route on 6/6 conditioned renders (deep_overflow_px=0); composition usable on a clear majority (5/6 PASS by the S7 worst-cell<=0.5 gate). The seed-1 'containment-not-fit' failure mode is now caught by the worst-cell gate and avoided by correct mask orientation.

mask_orientation.evidence: Natural orientation (notch bottom-right): median fit 68.3, 3/3 PASS, median worst-cell 0.38. Wrong orientation (notch top-right, prior session): median fit 39.1, 2/9 PASS, median worst-cell 0.71. Correct mask orientation nearly doubles median fit and lifts PASS from 22pct to 100pct -- the notch-top-right mask forced the axe handle onto the row center-line on almost every render.

T_hammer.evidence: War hammer (a genuine T-object: medial handle-to-head attachment) fits the T by translation: strict seed 603=95.89 (worst 0.0), 601=67.5; 2/3 PASS, deep 0. Subjects read a touch abstract (plain dark heads) but legible as hammers.

V2_auto_default.evidence: Awkward-shape half HOLDS: L strict median 68.3 vs off 32.5 (off seed 511 fit 4.88, deep_overflow 123 -- unusable); T strict 67.5 vs off 50.2. Strict rescues awkward footprints. BUT the 2x2 shield half REFUTES REQ-0186's rationale: strict median fit 81.3 (3/3 PASS) BEAT off median 71.8 (3/3 PASS), and strict did NOT flatten the shield into a plain disc -- it produced a characterful ROUND shield (boss, riveted rim, plank texture, weathering) filling the square, while off produced dynamic HEATER shields that leave the square corners emptier (the ~9pt fit gap). The GREEN criterion (off keeps character strict LOSES, at no fit cost) fails on both clauses.
V2_auto_default.note: auto->off is not catastrophic (off renders are attractive and more dynamic) but its DOCUMENTED justification is inaccurate, and off's silhouette is prompt-dependent (a detailed prompt drove off to a heater silhouette that underfills a full-rectangle cell). The now-working per-render override is the right tool for this per-item judgement; the blanket auto->off rule rests on a picture-level claim the pictures do not support.

V3_guide_honesty.evidence: Guide on the natural-L: median fit 53.4, 1/3 PASS, high variance (20.96 diagonal / 53.42 centered / 94.86 lucky). Sits between off (32.5) and strict (68.3), matching the docs (containment ~60pct, not legibility). Guide does NOT reliably read better than strict (1/3 PASS vs strict 3/3; its floor is a diagonal legibility failure). One lucky render beat strict, but that is the lottery guide is documented to be. Lock descriptions are honest.

V4_compare_workflow.evidence: Exercised the exact endpoints the artadmin UI calls: shield generated at off (701-703) and strict (711-713) via the one-shot generate override; params.shape_lock records off vs strict (attributable); artwork default stayed auto through both overrides (override did not mutate). PATCH {shape_lock:strict} changed the artwork default; existing render params untouched. Not driven through a browser (cannot); the operator's one-click lightbox compare + Save remains to eyeball in the live artadmin.

V5_ops.evidence: No OOM across 19 renders. VRAM peak observed ~5.5 GB (768x512 conditioned) -- LOWER than REQ-0153's 6.7-6.8 GB because the production route runs matting as a separate CPU inspection job, not co-resident on the GPU as the spike did. Cold-start first render ~700-880s wall (~508s model reload after REQ-0158 idle-free); warm conditioned 512x512 ~60-150s, 768x512 ~180s, plain off 512 ~90-120s.
V5_ops.note: 768x512 conditioned (~180s) runs above REQ-0153's 76-130s envelope -- expected for the larger canvas, not a recipe regression.

verdict.follow_up_req: Recommend a follow-up observation-only REQ: (1) correct REQ-0186 / item_content_pipeline.md S0.1 lock+auto wording -- strict does NOT flatten the shield into a plain disc; on the 2x2 it out-fit off (81.3 vs 71.8) while keeping character; (2) reconsider the auto rule premise for full rectangles -- off's bbox fill is prompt-dependent and can underfill, so auto->off on every full rectangle is a per-item judgement best left to the operator via the working override. Defaults NOT changed by this REQ (observation only).
